title: Astrid and the Landfall
premise: Riverboat captain Edmund Amberdale hauls a drowned chest from the Vellin River bearing the seal of Ostrava, a nation erased from maps twenty years ago. Inside are ledgers proving the republic's last magistrates hid evidence of a massacre ordered by the men who now rule the borderlands as respectable governors. Hunted by the Governor's private river police and betrayed by the scholar who hired him, Edmund must run the flooded gorges ahead of the monsoon to deliver the chest to an exiled judge in the delta city of Marrowgate. He arrives with his boat broken and half his crew gone, but the trial that follows — held outside any lawful court, on the deck of a beached gunship — convicts the Governor in the eyes of the river people, and Edmund finally stops measuring life in miles.
about_author: Yara Kavanagh is the pen name of a former barge hand who spent six seasons working inland waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about rivers, borders, and the people who live in the gaps between laws.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. After a night storm, the Vellin coughs up a lead-lined chest stamped with Ostrava's seal; Edmund, superstitious about drowned things, nearly rolls it back overboard. His deckhand Tamir convinces him to keep it until they find its owner. Beat: uneasy curiosity, the first crack in Edmund's careful distance from other people's histories.

chapters.title: A Passenger with Paper Hands
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At Corben's Landing, a pale archivist named Ilse Vant hires passage downriver, claiming the chest holds her family's records. Her hands shake when she touches the seal, and she lies badly about why. Edmund takes her money anyway — the boat needs caulking. Beat: transactional trust established on false pretenses.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Say
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Alone below decks, Ilse reads the magistrates' ledgers: names, dates, and orders for the Hollowing — the purge that ended Ostrava — signed by men who now hold governorships. She is not an archivist's daughter; she is the last magistrate's granddaughter. Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Grey Boats at Dusk
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Unmarked grey boats shadow the Amberdale through the narrows and signal them to heave to. Edmund runs the shallows instead, a maneuver only he knows, scraping paint and pride. Ilse admits someone wants the chest. Beat: the chase begins; Edmund chooses a side without admitting it.

chapters.title: The Toll at Weir Nine
chapters.summary: Tamir's POV. At the Weir Nine lock, a toll officer demands to inspect cargo and asks pointed questions about Ostrava. Tamir hides the ledgers inside a coffin bound for a delta funeral, lying smoothly for the first time in his honest life. Beat: complicity spreads; the crew becomes conspirators.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warnings
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Old pilot Maren reads the sky and gives them four days before the monsoon closes the gorges. Ilse reveals her true name and destination: Judge Anselm Rook, exiled in Marrowgate, the only living man empowered to convene a tribunal under old Ostravan law. Beat: stakes clarified — reach the delta or the evidence dies with them.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed
chapters.summary: Governor Cassel Bray's POV, first appearance. In his marble residence above the flood line, Bray reviews reports of the chest and remembers signing the order himself, young and ambitious. He dispatches Captain Ferro of the river police with instructions that leave no witnesses. Beat: the antagonist humanized and made more frightening by it.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Ferro's patrol boat catches them at dusk near the charcoal wharves; a running fight leaves the Amberdale holed and one pursuer burning. They escape into reed marshes, but Tamir takes a bullet through the shoulder. Beat: first blood; adventure turns costly.

chapters.title: Maren's Country
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren leads them to a hidden marsh settlement of river folk — smugglers, deserters, descendants of Ostravan refugees who never stopped telling stories. The community patches the hull and treats Tamir, and their elder recognizes the seal and weeps. Beat: Edmund discovers the past isn't dead, just submerged.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The marsh elders will guide them through the back channels, but demand the ledgers stay with the people if the mission fails — a copy, at least. Ilse refuses to divide the evidence; Edmund forces a compromise that satisfies no one. Beat: justice outside the law has its own politics.

chapters.title: Ferro's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ferro corners the Amberdale alone at a fuel depot and offers Edmund amnesty and gold to surrender the chest and the woman. Edmund counters by offering Ferro a look at page one — the signature. Ferro leaves without answering. Beat: the hunter wavers; corruption shown from inside.

chapters.title: Into the Gorges
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The monsoon's leading edge hits as they enter the flooded gorges: white water, rock gates, a rope-and-winch passage where the patched hull groans like something dying. Ilse works the winches beside the crew, earning her place. Beat: peak physical peril; trust forged in spray and terror.

chapters.title: Overboard
chapters.summary: Tamir's POV. A rogue wave sweeps the chest loose; Tamir goes in after it and Edmund dives after both. They lose the coffin-stowage trick and nearly each other, hauling the chest onto a gravel bar as the river tries to reclaim it. Beat: sacrifice made real; the chest becomes worth a life, which changes what carrying it means.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Halfway Light
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A marsh guide sells their position to Ferro for passage out of the flood zone. The ambush at Halfway Light costs Maren her life holding the tiller so the others can slip away downstream. Beat: grief and rage; the mentor falls so the mission can continue.

chapters.title: The Broken Boat
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With the engine flooded and the rudder cracked, they drift toward Marrowgate on jury-rigged sails made of awning canvas. Edmund confesses to Ilse why he measures life in miles: a wife and daughter lost to a fever town he sailed away from rather than stayed for. Beat: the captain's wound opened; miles versus years resolved emotionally.

chapters.title: Marrowgate Rising
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. They limp into the delta city as flood sirens sound; Ferro's boats wait at every legal berth. The river folk of Marrowgate, tipped by the marsh network, swarm the docks and hide the Amberdale inside a beached gunship scheduled for scrap. Beat: the lawless many shelter the just few.

chapters.title: Judge Rook
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. In a candlelit cabin aboard the hulk, they find Judge Anselm Rook — old, ill, and certain his court died with Ostrava. Ilse lays the ledgers before him and argues that a law survives as long as someone keeps faith with it. Rook agrees to convene a tribunal of river delegates. Beat: hope institutionalized outside the state.

chapters.title: The Trial on the Gunship
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Delegates from a dozen river communities hear testimony while Ferro's marines surround the hulk awaiting orders. Witnesses from the marsh settlement speak of the Hollowing's survivors; the ledgers' signatures are read aloud, including Bray's. Beat: climax of conscience — justice performed in public, unarmed.

chapters.title: Bray Comes Down to the Water
chapters.summary: Bray's POV. Rather than burn the hulk with everyone aboard, Bray descends to confront the tribunal personally, confident legality is on his side. Rook reads the massacre order into the record; the delegates pronounce judgment; Bray's own marines, river-born themselves, lower their rifles. Beat: power's corruption meets its limit — the men with guns choose.

chapters.title: After the Verdict
chapters.summary: Ferro's POV. Ordered to arrest the tribunal, Ferro instead arrests Bray on the old warrants the ledgers resurrect, choosing the law he can respect over the man who paid him. Bray is held for delivery to delta authorities; some justice, Ferro knows, will still leak away. Beat: imperfect resolution; the enforcer redeemed partially.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The monsoon peaks and recedes; the Amberdale, rebuilt by river volunteers, floats again. Ilse stays in Marrowgate to help Rook rebuild a court from the tribunal's bones; Tamir signs on as first mate. Edmund declines a commission and a medal alike. Beat: quiet aftermath; the cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Measuring in Years
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, closing. Spring high water: the Amberdale runs the Vellin again, ferrying pilgrims to the marsh memorial where Maren's name is carved beside the Hollowing's dead. Edmund passes the sandbar where the chest came up and, for the first time, thinks in years ahead instead of miles behind. Beat: full-circle resolution; memory kept, life resumed.
